thesis_statement: Deterrence Certainty Preference - The effectiveness of legal punishment in preventing crime depends more heavily on the perceived certainty of execution than the severity of the sanction
parent_thesis: Peano axioms
context_description: Criminological consensus indicating that utility-maximizing criminals are deterred by high probability of detection rather than abstract harsh sentences.

thesis_statement: Restorative Justice Restitution - Ethical justice requires the active restoration of emotional and physical harm through voluntary victim-offender reconciliation
parent_thesis: 1: Being (True)
context_description: A justice model shifting focus from retributive state punishment to repairing the social fabric and repairing relationships.

thesis_statement: Panopticon Self-Surveillance - The physical design of a prison that makes surveillance invisible forces inmates to internalize discipline, regulating their own behavior
parent_thesis: 1: Being (True)
context_description: Jeremy Bentham's architectural prison structure, analyzed by Foucault, illustrating the internalization of power and self-policing.

thesis_statement: Labeling Theory of Secondary Deviance - Applying formal criminal labels to individuals alters their social identity, driving them toward further criminal career paths
parent_thesis: 1: Being (True)
context_description: A sociological theory demonstrating that stigmatization and official classification can act as self-fulfilling prophecies, exacerbating criminal recidivism.

thesis_statement: Just Deserts Retribution - Punitive sentencing must be proportionally scaled to reflect the moral culpability of the offense, independent of utilitarian deterrence
parent_thesis: 1: Being (True)
context_description: The deontological retributive principle requiring that punishment is justified solely by the moral desert of the crime.
